pinboard.description:
(This website looks to have that “acoustic” flavor of someone whose special interest is Wi-Fi.)

“Wi-Fi’s first weakest link -- your client devices: Wi-Fi throughput to a Wi-Fi 5 wireless client device using an 80 MHz channel will likely max out at around 650 Mbps (±60 Mbps) for 2x2 MIMO no matter what new router is used when right next to the router; and slower at distance. And the far majority of ALL wireless client devices today (smartphones, tablets, laptops, etc) are still only 2x2 MIMO. So your Wi-Fi 5 client device [§4] is almost certainly causing ‘slow’ Wi-Fi PHY speeds (and maybe not your existing AP/router).

“For Wi-Fi 6 client devices, throughput can be around 1 Gbps 1201 Mbps PHY speed for an 80 MHz channel, provided your 2×2 client device is very close to the router, and even faster speeds (and an extended range for obtaining 1 Gbps) are possible with 160 MHz channels.”
